source.title: SAE-RNA: A Sparse Autoencoder Model for Interpreting RNA Language Model Representations

record.tranche_reason: The study trains SAEs and reports feature patterns across RiNALMo layers, but does not test whether increasing dictionary size splits features or whether the resulting features partition inputs and remain geometrically close.
record.gate_note: Each SAE has the same stated dictionary size (h = 10240); there is no dictionary-size sweep, smaller-versus-larger SAE comparison, parent/child feature matching, or test of whether child features partition a parent’s inputs. The reported layer-wise activation selectivity is adjacent to the claim but does not test any listed version. The reported SAE feature labels are not results about size-based splitting.
record.test_reason: The study trains one fixed-size SAE (h = 10240) per RiNALMo layer and labels features against RNA annotations. It has no dictionary-size sweep, no parent/child matching, no absorption test and no objective comparison, so it tests no version. It uses SAE decomposition as a tool, which fits T4 better than T6. The record's 'discusses'/T6 is close, but the paper does more than discuss: it applies SAEs without testing the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors frame SAE-RNA as an exploratory probe. Selected features align with stem/hairpin contexts and RNA family patterns, and deeper layers are more type-selective. They state the results do not establish biological concepts and that stability, length normalization and signal-versus-noise validation remain unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses conventional overcomplete SAEs on token-level RiNALMo embeddings, with one fixed dictionary size per layer; it does not compare dictionary sizes or test feature splitting.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that feature-level conclusions may depend on sparsity penalty, activation threshold, top-k selection, aggregation method, and layer selection; these choices are not systematically tested here.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE activation patterns are diffuse at layer 1, then sparser and more RNA-type-selective from layer 18 onward (qualitative, from heatmaps).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RiNALMo, SAE features become more concentrated and RNA-type-selective in deeper layers.

record.problems: The study does not systematically test the listed method choices; the layer-wise selectivity result is qualitative and based on heatmaps. The authors also note unresolved length-normalization, stability, and signal-versus-noise concerns.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size comparison, splitting, coverage of a parent's inputs, or direction similarity.
No size-based splitting test in large models or open SAE releases; a single SAE size is used on a 650M RNA model.
No feature families, nesting, geometry or hierarchy analysis.
No parent/child firing or absorption analysis, and no size or sparsity sweep.
No cross-size latent decomposition and no analysis of novel latents.
No comparison of training objectives (e.g. Matryoshka) and no correlated-input analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche are changed from discusses/T6 to uses_without_test/T4. The paper never mentions feature splitting or absorption. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of SAE dictionary sizes, feature splitting, input coverage, or direction similarity.
No size-based splitting test in large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested, geometrically close feature families or concept hierarchy.
No test of parent-child firing, absorption, or whether size or sparsity changes resolve it.
No comparison of latent combinations or novel latents across SAE sizes.
No test of whether the training objective produces splitting or whether Matryoshka or another objective changes it.

rows.subject: RiNALMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared RNA-type activation patterns from per-layer SAEs using top-k feature heatmaps with per-feature normalization and max aggregation.
rows.measure: Qualitative sparsity and RNA-type selectivity of SAE activation patterns
rows.value: From layer 18 onward, patterns are described as markedly sparser and more type-selective, remaining elevated with mild fluctuations through layer 33.
rows.note: This is a layer-depth comparison, not a dictionary-size or feature-splitting test. The text gives no numerical selectivity or sparsity values.
rows.check: This is a layer-depth comparison of qualitative sparsity and type selectivity at one fixed dictionary size, so it cannot show splitting. Its state relative to any version cannot be determined; 'observed' applies only to the study's own layer-wise finding, which is already recorded in fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
